We have long warned readers against sharing sensitive personal information in conversations with AI chatbots, given that most companies use these conversations as training data — but now there's a much more serious problem.

The situation escalated over the weekend, when Reddit users discovered that some Claude AI chat logs could be accessed through a simple Google search……

Claude Chat Logs Exposed

Claude offers a sharing feature that lets you share a chat log with colleagues, friends, or family. The chatbot generates a link you can send to one or more users, and Claude implicitly assures you that no one without the link can view the conversation.

The problem is that Reddit users discovered you don't actually need that link to view the chat. You can simply use Google, either by typing specific search terms, or by asking Google to show all chat logs shared this way. As BBC News reports:

You actually just need to tell Google to search the directory Claude uses for shared chat logs (site:claude.ai/share).

As you might expect, some of the chats are utterly bizarre — for example, someone asking why the music industry is hiding the fact that Jay-Z's albums are mostly ghostwritten by birds. But some contain extremely sensitive information, such as verbatim transcripts of private conversations; a lawyer asking whether they needed to proactively disclose a breach; and a user inadvertently revealing their private keys while seeking help setting up a cryptocurrency wallet.

Anthropic is still trying to claim this isn't a problem.

The fact is, this is clearly a serious problem, because it is absolutely not what users expected. Worse still, according to Wired, the root of the problem appears to be an extremely basic oversight.

This comes just one day after news that Claude Cowork was able to escape its sandbox environment and gain access to all files on a Mac.

How to Protect Yourself

The issue appears to have been at least partially addressed, as previously accessible search results have disappeared, but given that the sharing feature relies on the fragile design of "security through obscurity," I would still recommend avoiding it.

I also recommend deleting any previously shared chat logs. You can do this under "Settings > Privacy > Shared Chats > Manage."

Another vindication of Apple's privacy stance

Apple takes a three-tiered approach to privacy in Apple Intelligence and the new Siri:

  • On-device AI processing wherever possible
  • The first fallback is Apple's own Private Cloud Compute (PCC) servers
  • The final option is to use Gemini models equipped with equivalent PCC safeguards

The sophisticated PCC architecture means that neither Apple nor Google can access or retain any data. The security architecture Apple has designed allows for independent verification by security researchers.
